intro: Marginal frequencies alone can hide dependence between variables. A joint table reveals whether knowing one variable changes what to expect about the other.
task: Compute mutual information in nats from a normalized joint-probability matrix.
requirements: joint has shape (rows, columns), contains nonnegative values, and sums to one within absolute tolerance 1e-8.
Compute row and column marginals and sum joint_ij*log(joint_ij/(row_i*column_j)) over positive cells.
Zero rows and columns are allowed. They contribute nothing rather than causing division by zero.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Sum along each axis to find the two marginals; their product describes the independent model.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: For positive cells, subtract the two marginal logarithms from the joint logarithm to avoid underflowing their product.

explanation: Independence predicts each cell as the product of its two marginal probabilities. Mutual information is the KL divergence from the observed joint table to that independence model.
Perfect agreement between two fair binary variables carries log(2) nats of information. Independent variables have zero mutual information even when their marginal probabilities are unequal.
